newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana chooses Sask for electricity joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Guyana chooses Sask for electricity joint venture.

text.p: Canada's Sask Power, wholly-owned subsidiary of Saskatchewan Power Corp, has been chosen by Guyana to negotiate a joint venture with ailing Guyana Electricity Corporation (GEC), Prime Minister Sam Hinds said.
The Canadian firm was picked among three bidders for a proposed 50-50 partnership with GEC, he told reporters.
Hinds said Sask Power proposed a bid worth $22.6 million for a 50 percent stake in state-run GEC. The government was initially seeking between $35 and $45 million.

The Guyanese government agreed to take up the offer, Hinds said, because "we have an opportunity for someone to bring the capital required to make the GEC into an operation that can give reliable electricity at about the lowest possible prices."

Johan Van't Hof, Managing Director of Price Waterhouse, Toronto Corporate Finance, the investment consultants to Guyana on the deal, said the investment would reach about $30 million when other factors are taken into consideration.

The deal is scheduled to be concluded by end-March. If Sask were unable to go through with it, Hinds said the offer would be made to the second best bidder, Leucadia National Corp of the United States.
Foreign diplomats and economic experts say the fate of GEC, which partially collapsed in 1995, is paramount in a country that has been plagued by a deficient supply of electric power for years.
